away.headline: Colts elevate LB Germaine Pratt, CB Kenneth Harris from practice squad to active roster; release P Thomas Morstead from practice squad
away.blurb: Colts elevate LB Germaine Pratt, CB Kenneth Harris from practice squad to active roster; release P Thomas Morstead from practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The roster moves were made Saturday. The Indianapolis Colts today elevated cornerback Kenneth Harris and linebacker Germaine Pratt to the active roster from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. The team also released punter Thomas Morstead from the practice squad. Harris , 6-0, 192 pounds, was elevated in Week 1 vs. Baltimore and registered one solo tackle. He was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. Harris participated in training camp with the Colts after originally signing with the team as a free agent on August 26, 2026. He previously participated in the New England Patriots' 2026 offseason program and training camp. Harris was originally signed by the Patriots as an undrafted free agent on May 8, 2026. Collegiately, he played in 59 career games (29 starts) at Oklahoma State (2023-25) and Arkansas State (2020-22) and compiled 113 tackles (92 solo), 61.5 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack, 28 passes defensed and three interceptions. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 13, 2026. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025-26), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Pratt began last season with the Raiders, where he started four games and recorded 25 tackles (10 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss and two passes defensed. Morstead , 6-4, 225 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 20, 2026. He has played in 272 career games in his time with the Colts (2026), San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). Morstead has registered 1,004 punts for 46,863 yards (46.7 avg./41.3 net avg.) with 374 pinned inside the 20-yard line. He has also totaled 263 touchbacks on kickoffs. Morstead has appeared in 18 postseason contests and has compiled 64 punts for 2,821 yards (44.1 avg./40.8 net avg.) with 22 pinned inside the 20-yard line. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Colts, they have seven starters who did not practice Wednesday due to injury. They include linebacker Bryce Boettcher, cornerback Sauce Gardner, right guard Matt Gonglaves, punter Rigoberto Sanchez, right tackle Jalen Travis, slot cornerback Justin Walley, and tight end Tyler Warren. Slot Cornerback Justin Walley's injury is new. Not much else is known at this point, but his not practicing and Sauce Gardner already likely out on Sunday could leave the Colts' struggling secondary pretty thin at cornerback. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. The Miami Dolphins are traveling up the East Coast this weekend for an AFC East showdown with the New York Jets on Sunday at MetLife Stadium. On Saturday, the Dolphins made their final roster moves for Week 7, as they activated linebacker Kyle Louis from injured reserve and elevated kicker Zane Gonzalez and defensive end Max Llewellyn from the practice squad. Louis, 22, played at Pittsburgh from 2022-25, earning All-ACC honors twice and All-American honor once. Miami took him in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL draft. In Week 1, Louis played 17 total snaps (three on defense and 14 on special teams), but he suffered a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve. Gonzalez, 31, is in his eighth season in the NFL, and he's made 81% of his field goals and 95.3% of his extra points in his career, while playing for the Arizona Cardinals, Cleveland Browns, Carolina Panthers, Atlanta Falcons and Washington Commanders. He takes Riley Patterson's place on the gameday roster. This article originally appeared on Dolphins Wire: Dolphins activate LB from IR, elevate 2 players from practice squad

away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. Malik Willis wants fewer turnovers Quarterback Malik Willis has 4 interceptions and 5 fumbles in his first 5 games with the team. He was listed on the Injury Report with an injured right thumb, but has been practicing all week and will start. "It just can't happen, you know?" Willis said. "I mean, regardless of what went down to force the turnovers, you just can't have them, regardless. away.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

away.blurb: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said running back Breece Hall would not practice Wednesday because of a quadriceps injury, although Hall had not been ruled out for Sunday. Braelon Allen has led New York with 314 rushing yards on 74 carries and would remain the primary back if Hall cannot play. Receiver Adonai Mitchell was expected to practice on a limited basis because of a finger injury. Left guard Dylan Parham is dealing with a knee injury. Edge rusher Joseph Ossai has an ankle problem, linebacker Kiko Mauigoa has a leg issue and slot corner Jarvis Brownlee Jr. has been monitored in the concussion process. Tight end Mason Taylor also appears on the Jets' broader injury watch with a thumb issue. Miami's most important offensive injury involves Jonah Savaiinaea . The starting right guard returned to limited work Monday after injuring his ankle against Cincinnati. Jarrett Kingston played well in relief and is the likely replacement if Savaiinaea cannot handle a full workload. Receiver Caleb Douglas also returned on a limited basis Monday after missing time with an ankle injury. His availability would add size and speed to a group led by Malik Washington, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr. Cornerback JuJu Brents is recovering from a neck injury or stinger, safety Michael Taaffe has a chest concern, cornerback Reese Taylor has dealt with a quadriceps injury and edge rusher Robert Beal Jr. has been limited by a hamstring problem. Tight end Justin Joly remains a concussion question. Quarterback Malik Willis is expected to play after tending to a minor undisclosed issue coming out of the Cincinnati game. Miami also may receive help from players eligible to return from reserve lists, including cornerbacks Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr. and edge defender Trey Moore. Eligibility does not guarantee activation, but those decisions could address thin positions. Wednesday participation is only the first checkpoint. Thursday will show whether limited players progress, and Friday will provide the official game designations. home.blurb: As is always the case in the NFL, the injury report will be watched throughout the coming days until kickoff. Ahead of the Sunday game scheduled for 1 p.m. at MetLife Stadium, the Jets (2-4) have a few names that will be watched. Some of the top ones include running back Breece Hall ( quad ) wide receiver AD Mitchell (finger) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). home.headline: Caleb Douglas could return to Miami Dolphins lineup against New York Jets
home.blurb: “Caleb will be limited [in practice] today. You know, we’ll see how he looks today and progress to Wednesday, but I think there’s optimism there. Let’s see how it goes today, and if he can get ramped up on Wednesday, it would be good to get him back out there.” The Miami Dolphins had a much needed bye week this past weekend. Multiple players have been banged up, including standout rookie receiver Caleb Douglas. It seems the added rest has been a good thing for the young pass catcher, as according to head coach Jeff Hafley, Douglas has a chance to suit up against the New York Jets on the road this upcoming Sunday. During his press availability on Monday morning, head coach Jeff Hafley was asked about Douglas’ potential to practice this week. Hafley, with a smile on his face, would go on to speak about what Miami missed on offense without Douglas in the mix. “Just kind of looking back through the last couple of weeks, some of the things that he did, we’ve missed him. And to see a rookie kind of have to start and stop like that, not ideal. But, he’s worked really hard and it would be very great to get him back.” We will keep a close eye on Douglas’ practice participation as the week unfolds, but as of Monday afternoon, his availability seems to be pointing in a positive direction in regards to playing this Sunday.

home.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is cleared to play in the upcoming game against the New York Jets on Sunday. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. away.headline: Will Jaelan Phillips play against the Buccaneers in Week 7?
away.blurb: Jaelan Phillips has officially been ruled out of the Week 7 matchup with a hamstring injury, according to the Panthers' final injury report . Phillips did not practice Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday, and head coach Dave Canales said earlier in the week the team was preparing to play without him. The Panthers will also be without edge rusher Thomas Incoom, who was ruled out with a calf injury after missing all three practices. Baker Mayfield is expected to return after missing three games with a dislocated right thumb, but the Buccaneers will miss starting right tackle Luke Goedeke with a calf injury. Even with Phillips sidelined, protecting Mayfield remains a priority for an offense that allowed five sacks against Pittsburgh last week. But his return from a thumb injury isn't so simple. With his thumb injury being on his throwing hand, playing quarterback might be a bit tricky. But he recently got some help. Rays helped Baker Mayfield with custom glove amid return from thumb injury While the Rays are focused on winning the World Series, Bond was able to help out the city's NFL team by designing a new glove to help Mayfield play through a thumb injury. According to Rick Stroud of The Tampa Bay Times , the Tampa Bay Rays actually helped design a new custom glove for Mayfield's right hand leading up to Week 7 to try to help him play without any complications. But how did the Rays help make this glove for Mayfield to suit up in Week 7 against the Panthers in a must-win matchup? home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. Meanwhile, Cincy is coming out of a bye week and is in a prime spot to make a run up the AFC North standings. After this game, the Bengals take on Tennessee, Atlanta, Pittsburgh, Washington and New Orleans (four teams under .500) to close out October and November. Baltimore opened as a 3-point favorite , but the Bengals were favored on Wednesday after Jackson was limited in practice. The total has moved down from 50.5 to 48.5. Bengals vs. Ravens Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking the Bengals to cover on the road: As I've written about already in this article, this is the week when I really start looking at strength of schedule, betting against teams who have had it easy through the first six weeks and betting on teams who have had it tough. No one has had it easier than the Baltimore Ravens, who have started their season against the Colts, Saints, Cowboys, Titans, Falcons, and Browns. Now they'll face their best competition yet, the Bengals, who are going to be feeling fresh off their bye. Lamar Jackson's status for this game is up in the air, but we can assume, based on the betting line, that the market believes he'll play. If he does sit out, we're going to end up with a great line with Cincinnati +3. The Bengals are seventh in EPA per play and 13th in opponent EPA per play while playing a much more difficult schedule than the Ravens. I think they can at least keep this game within a field goal, if not win it outright. Jackson’s status obviously could swing this game, but the Ravens haven’t exactly had to face a tough path in the 2026 season. Meanwhile, Cincy is coming out of a bye and is ninth in the NFL in EPA/Play on offense. Burrow and Co. should make things tough on a Ravens team that struggled a bit against Atlanta and wasn’t able to come up with enough stops in losses to New Orleans and Cleveland. The margin for error for the Ravens becomes much thinner if Jackson doesn’t play, or if he’s not 100 percent. I like Cincy to get an upset win on Sunday. Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson did get in some “limited” work today. https://t.co/3rq60qmJVB The Ravens opened as three-point favorites at home in this massive Week 7 matchup against AFC North foe, and that line bounced around from 2.5 to 3 in the lead up to Wednesday's practice. However, Jackson was not spotted at the beginning of practice and was later seen walking off with a limp. As a result, oddsmakers at DraftKings quickly shifted the odds in this game to Bengals -1.5, a huge 4.5-point flip from where they were entering the week. Lamar Jackson (ankle) seen walking off practice field with a limp, per @CordellWoodland . https://t.co/1R708hsFHo That's a sign that Jackson isn't expected to play in Week 7, and he may need to log a full practice on Thursday or Friday to shift the sentiment in the betting market. Sports Illustrated spoke to multiple oddsmakers this week about how they set the line for a game like this with Jackson's status up in the air. "Your lookahead line, you essentially have to assume he's going to play until you hear otherwise.," Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook, told Sports Illustrated. "So, that's baked into the price, whether we anticipate he'll be at full strength or 80% strength, that would kind of be factored in there. "And then, as the week goes on, we'll adjust as we know more. Obviously, he wasn't at practice today, and our line went down a point and a half just off that alone. And then we'll kind of trickle down as the week goes on and his status becomes more and more certain one way or the other. If he's back at practice tomorrow in a limited or full capacity, the line will probably shift back towards the Ravens. If he's not there again on Thursday, we'll essentially start pricing as though [Tyler] Huntley is going to be the starter." So, what could the line close at if Huntley makes his third start in a row? "If he's out and it's Huntley again, the line will most likely shift to the Bengals being the favorite, probably in that 1.5 to 2.5 range," Gour said. So, based on Gour's projection, the current line suggest that Jackson won't play. That would be a huge blow to a Ravens team that is 4-2 and already lost a division game in Week 6. In his four games this season, Jackson completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score while leading the NFL in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating. The Ravens are 7-12 all time without Jackson, though they've won three of the four starts Huntley has made in his place since the 2025 season. Bettors are going to want to monitor Baltimore's practice report on Thursday, as it could solidify Jackson's status for Sunday's game. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. As for the Baltimore Ravens , their kicker is on notice. These teams meet in a Week 7 AFC North clash, and here are bold predictions for the contest. The Bengals (3-2) enter the game in last place in the division despite having a winning record. That's because the Ravens, Steelers, and surprising Browns all have a record of 4-2. It should be another battle for the Ravens and Bengals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.headline: Lamar Jackson injury update: Ravens QB to miss third straight game against Bengals in Week 7
away.blurb: Lamar Jackson ruled out vs Bengals However, Baltimore will once again be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson, who has been ruled out of the matchup because of an ankle injury. "QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to “out” for tomorrow’s game vs. Cincinnati," the team announced on Saturday, Although the quarterback participated in limited practice sessions this week, the team confirmed on Saturday that he would not be available against Cincinnati. Jackson’s return to the practice field offered some encouragement, but the Ravens remained cautious about declaring him fully fit for Sunday’s game. The 29-year-old was listed as “questionable” on Friday’s injury report, with Minter suggesting that his availability could be decided shortly before kickoff. However, the Ravens ultimately made the decision earlier. Jackson details key return factor The Ravens quarterback also clarified that managing the pain would be more important than the reduction in swelling when assessing his readiness to return to action. The Baltimore Ravens will face the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday in Week 7 of the NFL season as they look to recover from last week’s defeat to the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens split their last two games against the Atlanta Falcons and Cleveland Browns without Jackson. Ravens cautious about Jackson’s recovery "He's been able to get some work in these past couple of days," Ravens coach Jesse Minter confirmed on Friday. "Between Lamar and our staff, it's going to be a decision based on him and how he feels and how effective it could be. He's had a good couple of days, but we'll see how it goes over the next 48 hours,” the coach had mentioned. Jackson was sidelined from practice for two weeks after suffering the injury in Week 4. However, he provided an optimistic update on Friday, telling reporters that his recovery was “headed in the right direction.” "I feel like the swelling went down a lot. It's just the pain tolerance. Just trying to move how I move. If I can't do that, I can't help my team,” he said. Ravens’ starting QB in Jackson’s absence With Jackson sidelined again, Tyler Huntley is expected to take over as Baltimore’s starting quarterback. Huntley would start his third game of the season in place of the injured Jackson, continuing his role as Baltimore’s temporary starting quarterback. He has performed reliably in relief, avoiding interceptions across three appearances and posting a 1-1 record in his two previous starts.

away.headline: Bengals get big chance after final Lamar Jackson injury update
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: No more speculation about Lamar Jackson’s injury . No mind games that run up to kickoff on Sunday. Nothing. Just Jackson’s ankle injury being so bad that the Ravens decided to simply rule him out on Saturday by downgrading him to out. The Cincinnati Bengals couldn’t ask for a better situation going into the Week 7 encounter with the Baltimore Ravens. In for Jackson will be Tyler Huntley, who has gone 1-1 over his last two, throwing for three scores in the process. As Bengals fans will remember, it was Huntley who started against the Bengals in the playoffs in 2022, throwing two touchdowns and one score, but having the fumble that Sam Hubbard returned 98 yards for a score to swing the outcome. If the Bengals can take advantage of this on the road, they could move to 4-2 and jump the Ravens, if not others, in the AFC North. away.headline: Lamar Jackson Out for Ravens vs. Bengals, Latest Updates on QB's Ankle Injury
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals, the team announced Saturday. Jackson was previously listed as questionable heading into Baltimore's Week 7 matchup due to a a high ankle sprain. He was a limited participant in practice on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday ahead of the AFC North clash. "Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson told reporters Friday. "I can't call it right now, still got a grace period. We'll see, man, hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." He initially suffered the ankle sprain during Baltimore's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. The Ravens have turned to backup quarterback Tyler Huntley in Jackson's absence, and will do so again Sunday. Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5 before falling to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

away.headline: Lamar Jackson injury: Ravens star out for Week 7 vs. Bengals
away.blurb: Jackson returned to practice earlier this week, for the first time since suffering the injury in the second half against Tennessee, but has been officially ruled out by the Ravens ahead of Sunday’s clash with their AFC North rivals the Cincinnati Bengals. The Baltimore Ravens will be without Lamar Jackson for the third consecutive week, as the quarterback continues working his way back from a high-ankle sprain he suffered back in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. After practicing this week, Jackson spoke with the media about the injury : “I just know it was a sprain, and it hurt bad,” Jackson said as quoted by the official Ravens website. “It was very, very, very, very, very painful. “Just trying to move how I move,” Jackson said. “If I can’t do that, I can’t help my team. I can’t put my team in a situation to win. I feel like I’m doing a disservice, if anything.” Tyler Huntley stepped in for Jackson against Tennessee, and led the Ravens to an overtime win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5. While Huntley was fairly sharp against Atlanta, completing 24-of-32 passes for 201 yards and a pair of touchdowns in the 30-23 win, he completed just 19-of-31 passes for 165 yards and a touchdown as the Ravens lost to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.

away.headline: Lamar Jackson Injury Status Revealed Ahead of Bengals-Ravens Showdown
away.source: Cincinnati Bengals On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The Ravens have announced that Jackson will be out in Sunday's contest against the Bengals. The former league MVP is dealing with an ankle injury that has sidelined him for the last two games. The Cincinnati Bengals are on the eve of what will be one of their biggest games of the season. On Sunday, the Bengals are on the road as they look to keep pace in the AFC North in a battle against the Baltimore Ravens. Coming off of a bye week, the Bengals are looking up at every other team in the division. A win on Sunday puts the Bengals in a place where they could control their own destiny. Winning in Baltimore is a tall task. It's even taller when Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is in the lineup. However, the latest injury report from the Ravens may just change the Bengals' game plan. In four games this season, Jackson has posted a 3-1 starting record and has thrown for 967 yards, six touchdown passes, and just one interception. Obviously, the Ravens not having Jackson is a brutal blow for them. However, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley has been very serviceable since hearing his name called. In two starts since becoming the starter for the Ravens, Huntley is 1-1, with a win over the Atlanta Falcons and a loss last week to the Cleveland Browns. Huntley has done an outstanding job protecting the football in his two starts, throwing zero interceptions. However, he could be facing one of the most dynamic defensive lines he has seen in his short time under center. Putting pressure in Huntley may be the key to winning the game for the Bengals. Interior defensive linemen Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen may very well be the biggest offseason acquisitions the Bengals have made in quite some time. It's not just the interior of the defensive line that has impressed this season for the Bengals. Another offseason acquisition, Boye Mafe, has been a shining star on the edge. The Bengals are tied for the sixth most sacks in the NFL this season at 17, and aside from the Detroit Lions, who lead the league in sacks, every team ahead of Cincinnati on the list has played more games this season. There's a lot on the line Sunday, and the Ravens are going to have to go to war without their best soldier against a Bengals team that is starving to get back on the field. The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. During the Bengals' matchup with the Ravens, Cincinnati will be seeking to extend its record to 4-2, which is what all three of the other AFC North teams currently remain tied at going into Week 7. However, due to the early bye week, the Bengals currently sit at 3-2, putting them last in the division. Before the injury news came down, the matchup had been widely anticipated as the toughest test yet for Cincinnati's newly revamped defensive line, with Jackson named as the league MVP for the 2019 and 2023 seasons. However, Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense are still expected to be in for quite a defensive challenge from the Ravens on Sunday: As the Bengals take to the field at M&T Bank Stadium, it will mark the first time that Burrow will face off against Trey Hendrickson on an opposing team's defensive line. This comes after the star edge rusher, who led the NFL in sacks in 2024, left Cincinnati last year for Baltimore following a prolonged contract dispute with the Bengals front office. The game kicks off at 1 p.m. in Baltimore. Read more about this week's biggest storylines going into the game here. home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens and their fans are in for another 24 hours or so of nervous waiting as 2-time NFL MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson heads into a game-time decision on whether he will play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7. Jackson had a noticeable limp when he walked out to speak with the media following Friday's practice. "In his career, when Jackson has missed four or fewer gaem "Ravens OC Declan Doyle says the team can wait until GAME TIME to decide whether Lamar Jackson is ready to start against Cincinnati," Ravens Nation Live wrote on its official X account on Saturday. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. Going to venerated Wembley Stadium, facing off against the division-leading Jaguars, who had the advantage of having played in England the week prior and didn't have to worry about their body clocks, and managing to get away with a win was huge for the Texans. Houston, now at 2-4 but having won two straight road games against division rivals, returns to NRG Stadium to host the New York Giants of New Jersey. The Giants, sitting at 3-2-1, come into this matchup atop the NFC East, despite not winning in their last two games, a tie at Washington and a loss against New Orleans. In their last game, they fell to the Saints 34-27, but the Saints held a lead of 34-10 at one point in the 4th Quarter. The Giants, forced to start backup QB Jameis Winston since starter Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, decided to give recent trade acquisition J.J. The New York/New Jersey sports pages will have themselves a field day talking about the QB spot in this coming week. Likely because of that QB uncertainty, along with Houston's recent winning streak and the supposed talent disparity, the opening odds from FanDuel for the upcoming matchup between the Texans and the Giants are strongly supporting Houston at home: Overall, this may seem a bit high of an opening line. The Giants haven't played as difficult a schedule as Houston and they are coming in with key injuries and roster concerns. However, the Texans, even coming off a huge win against Jacksonville, are still struggling on defense and sit at 0-3 at home. They have only beaten the Giants once in 6 total meetings, and that was in 2002. Sandwiched between an international game and a bye week, this has the feel of a trap game for Houston. This particular line may tighten a bit as the week progresses, especially as the Giants sort out their QB situation and both teams sort out their respective injury situations. The Houston Texans' Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants is sitting right around the corner. And it's a game that, for the Texans, could hold some pretty high stakes for a few reasons. They're back at home after a trip over the pond to London, they'll be looking to keep their recent momentum going to stamp a third-straight victory in the books, and of course, this game will mark wide receiver Tank Dell's first game back on the field since his knee injury suffered in December of 2024. The Houston home crowd will be hungry for a win, and as will the Texans' roster in order to head into the bye on a high note. But just how will the Texans and Giants' actions end up unraveling this Sunday? Last week, Marks combined for over 80 yards from scrimmage against a Jacksonville Jaguars run defense that stands among the best in the league. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson goes runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. away.headline: Broncos elevate S Taylor Rapp and CB/KR Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad
away.blurb: According to 9NEWS Denver's Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are elevating veteran safety Taylor Rapp and return specialist/cornerback Sam Fresch Jr. from the practice squad for Sunday's game vs. the Arizona Cardinals. As for Sam Fresch Jr., he will provide depth at cornerback and in the kicking game as a returner. With star cornerback Pat Surtain II listed as questionable, the elevation of Fresch Jr. seems to put his status trending in the wrong direction for tomorrow's game vs. the Cardinals. Surtain II practiced on a limited basis all week, but the team could decide to hold him out for one more week in hopes of having him ready for next Sunday's key divisional matchup vs. the Kansas City Chiefs. If Surtain II does not go, look for Riley Moss to be 100% and start with Jahdae Barron filling in for Surtain II for the third straight week. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scotty Payne Sat, October 24, 2026 at 8:49 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Rapp started and played significant snaps in place of veteran starting safety Talanoa Hufanga, who was sidelined with an injury last week vs. the Seahawks and will do the same this week vs. the Cardinals. The experienced veteran played well in his first game with the Broncos and will be called on to do the same this week vs. the Cardinals. This is the second of the max three practice squad elevations for Rapp, so he can be elevated one more time before he will need to be added to the 53-man roster in order to play. According to reports, Talanoa Hufanga is expected back next Sunday vs. the rival Kansas City Chiefs, but we will need to wait and see how he progresses throughout the week. Still, we will need to keep an eye on his status in the lead-up to tomorrow's game vs. the Cardinals. So, look for Rapp to get the start once again tomorrow at safety, and we will need to keep an eye on the status of star cornerback Pat Surtain II prior to the game tomorrow. If he cannot go, Fresch Jr. will provide depth at corner for the Broncos, while Jahdae Barron will likely get another start in place of the sidelined Surtain.

away.headline: Broncos’ Pat Surtain and Jonah Coleman questionable against Cardinals, Talanoa Hufanga out
away.blurb: Surtain practiced in limited fashion throughout the week Pat Surtain II is listed as questionable with an ankle injury ahead of the Broncos' Week 7 matchup in Arizona. The All-Pro cornerback missed Denver's Week 5 and 6 matchups after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4 against the San Francisco 49ers. The Broncos chose not to place the cornerback on injured reserve, suggesting a possible return either this week or next Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. away.headline: Broncos injury report: Pat Surtain, Jonah Elliss, Talanoa Hufanga, Jonah Coleman updates
away.blurb: Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain ( ankle ) and wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) were limited while safety Talanoa Hufanga ( ankle ), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss ( ankle ) and running back Tyler Badie ( thumb ) did not participate. Surtain has missed the team's last two games, and it sounds like he might also miss Week 7 , but returning to practice is a good step in the right direction. Hufanga is likely going to miss at least one more game after sitting out last week's contest. Jahdae Barron and Taylor Rapp have done a nice job stepping up in the secondary while PS2 and Hufanga have been sidelined. Denver coach Sean Payton indicated Elliss avoided a season-ending injury , but he seemed to hint that Elliss could land on short-term injured reserve later this week. Meanwhile, Cooper is expected to return to the active roster this week after being reinstated by the NFL . Badie injured his thumb in the second quarter of last Thursday's game, and he was ruled out just before halftime. Meanwhile, Coleman is eligible to return from injured reserve this week, and he returned to practice on Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to be activated to the 53-man roster. away.headline: Injury Report: Week 7 vs Broncos
away.blurb: The team ruled out right guard Jon Gaines II and defensive tackle Walter Nolen III. Gaines suffered the knee/ankle injury during practice on Thursday. They will turn to Hayden Conner to play right guard. Nolen hurt his ankle last week against the Rams. On Friday, coach Mike LaFleur said they are monitoring the status of Budda Baker (groin/illness), Max Melton (knee), and Darius Robinson (back). All three are questionable to play. Quarterback Carson Beck is also questionable to play with back spasms. The Broncos will be without safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle), and running back Tyler Badie (thumb). Cornerback Pat Surtain II is questionable to play. After being a limited participant on Wednesday due to a knee injury, cornerback Max Melton didn't on Thursday, one of six players not in attendance. The others were defensive lineman Walter Nolen III (ankle), running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle), quarterback Carson Beck (back), and safeties Dewey Wingard (knee) and Budda Baker (Illness/Groin). Cornerback Garrett Williams (knee) did return on Thursday after missing the previous day, which was an encouraging sign. Defensive lineman Darius Robinson and right guard Jon Gaines II appeared on the injury report as limited. Robinson is dealing with a back issue while Gaines was listed with a knee. After injuring his right ankle against the Rams, Walter Nolen III did not practice. It was another DNP for Dewey Wingard as he works through the knee injury he sustained against the Giants. LaFleur did not rule out any of the three players for the game. Safety Wydett Williams Jr. was wearing the yellow non-contact bib during practice following his concussion. Quarterback Carson Beck was not throwing the football around during the open portion of practice. Cornerback Max Melton (knee) joined Williams and Beck as limited, Denver's safety Talanoa Hufanga did not practice with an ankle injury. Cornerback Pat Surtain II was limited with an ankle problem as well. away.headline: Broncos have 7 players on injured reserve going into Week 7
away.blurb: Four of those players — wide receiver Pat Bryant ( ankle ), running back Jonah Coleman ( ankle ), offensive tackle Frank Crum and tight end Caleb Lohner — are on short-term injured reserve, which means they are eligible to return after four games (although Lohner is expected to be out until at least mid-season ). Coleman is eligible to return from IR this week , and outside linebacker Jonah Elliss might be a candidate for IR after he was spotted using a walking boot and crutches over the weekend. Another player, offensive lineman Nick Gargiulo , is on the reserve/physically unable to perform (PUP) list. He is also eligible to return after four games. home.blurb: The Cardinals have ruled out all of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Andrew Wingard (knee), Walter Nolen III (ankle) and Jon Gaines (knee) ahead of Sunday's clash at State Farm Stadium. Budda Baker (groin/illness), Carson Beck (back), Max Melton (knee) and Darius Robinson (back) are officially listed as questionable. Both teams are able to make up to two standard practice squad elevations on Saturday, which could tip who is probable to play or not play depending on which positions are activated. The Cardinals are desperately looking to play spoiler once again, though some massive injuries in the likes of Nolen and Love will make things tough. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. away.headline: Packers Coach Matt LaFleur Gives Latest Micah Parsons Injury Update
away.blurb: However, Parsons didn't compete in Sunday night's matchup against his former team, the Dallas Cowboys, and it seems that he won't be available to play any time soon. This doesn't come as a huge surprise after NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported over the weekend that Parsons isn't expected to return to the field until Week 9 against the New England Patriots on Nov. 8 at the earliest . But, there's a good chance the Packers will hold him out until after their bye week, which will be in Week 11. That would mean Parsons could wait to make his season debut until the Thanksgiving eve game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons was originally expected to make his 2026 season debut in Week 6 after his long journey from tearing his ACL and meniscus last year in Week 15. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Monday that Parsons will not practice this week, meaning he won't be ready to go for Week 7's game versus the Detroit Lions , an NFC North rival for Green Bay. "He's got to clear some hurdles yet to get to that point," LaFleur said. The Packers will have to open Parsons's 21-day practice window before fans can even expect him to get close to playing. Waiting another month-plus for Parsons's debut would not be ideal for the Packers. Green Bay traded for Parsons last season, and so far, they've only had him play in 14 games across the two seasons. The team is still waiting to reap the full benefits of acquiring Parsons. It's unclear what the hold-up is for Parsons, but he hasn't been medically cleared yet.

away.headline: Packers Week 7 injury report vs. Lions: Are Christian Watson, Matthew Golden injuries cause for concern?
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers have reason for concern at wide receiver entering Week 7 against the Detroit Lions , but the available injury report does not justify assuming Christian Watson or Matthew Golden will miss the matchup. Watson, dealing with an ankle injury, and Golden, managing a shoulder issue, were limited participants Wednesday and Thursday. Neither progressed to full participation across those sessions, although neither was listed as a nonparticipant. They are officially questionable coming into this Week 7 matchup. For Green Bay, the concern centers on potential limitations and thinning receiver depth, not confirmed absences. Still, two limited practices cannot establish how effectively he can accelerate, separate or handle a full workload. Those remain football questions, not conclusions supported by the participation designations alone. The most encouraging offensive development belongs to Jordan Love. Listed with a back injury, the quarterback advanced from limited participation Wednesday to full participation Thursday. Savion Williams also remained limited Wednesday and Thursday because of an ankle injury. Taken together, those four receiver listings create a broader preparation problem. Guard Aaron Banks was limited both days with knee and toe injuries, adding another offensive situation to monitor before any availability assessment becomes definitive. Green Bay’s defensive report contains several unresolved situations. Defensive tackles Anthony Campbell and Jordon Riley were limited Wednesday and Thursday with ankle and Achilles injuries, respectively. Zaire Franklin appeared as limited Thursday with a shin injury after no Wednesday injury listing. Lukas Van Ness similarly moved onto the report Thursday as limited because of illness. Those additions deserve attention, but the available information does not establish their game availability. His ability to threaten downfield can influence safety positioning and create space for other receivers. His production reinforces that importance. Through six games, Watson has 29 receptions for 538 yards and six touchdowns, averaging approximately 18.6 yards per catch. Removing that explosive element would change how Green Bay attacks Detroit. Golden’s shoulder injury creates uncertainty. His 30 catches for 501 yards and three touchdowns through six games show how much production Green Bay would risk losing if his availability becomes restricted. For a receiver, the practical concern is whether discomfort affects catching, extending for throws or handling contact. However, the report provides no diagnosis beyond “shoulder” and no evidence establishing those limitations. Both players practicing in some capacity is preferable to consecutive absences.
