away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. home.headline: Lions officially activate DB Brian Branch, C Cade Mays
home.blurb: The Lions listed both players as questionable on Friday's injury report, but removed them after being activated. The team plans to start Mays at center instead of reserve Juice Scruggs and add Branch to a slumping secondary. "Cade and Branch are doing good here," Campbell said on Friday. The Packers officially activated former All-Pro running back Josh Jacobs, who spent the first six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list, for the contest, along with defensive tackle Jordon Riley. The Lions expected Jacobs to make his season debut . "Obviously that's going to boost everything," defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said. "Everybody's just looking at the run game. home.headline: Will Jordan Love, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden play vs. Lions?
home.blurb: Love dealt with back soreness coming out of last Sunday night's win over the Dallas Cowboys. While limited during Wednesday's walk-through practice, Love got in full practices on both Thursday and Friday and is good to go for Sunday. He never believed he was in danger of missing the important NFC North showdown with the Lions. The only player the Packers ruled out on the final injury report of Week 7 was linebacker Zaire Franklin, who is dealing with a shin injury. Quarterback Jordan Love and receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden do not have a status designation on the final injury report released Friday and will play against the Lions. Watson (ankle) and Golden (shoulder) both had new injuries to start the week, but neither missed practice during the week and both are off the injury report ahead of Sunday. Their injuries can be considered minor. The Packers need all three players at their best in a potential shootout with the Lions at Ford Field. The offense's passing attack has been a strength of the Packers, with Love ranking third in the NFL in passing yards entering Week 7, while both Watson (fifth) and Golden (sixth) rank in the top six players in receiving yards. Running back Josh Jacobs, who missed the first six games while on the exempt list, practiced all three days this week and is expected to play against the Lions. picks.headline: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football College football updates NFL injury updates Brewers take Game 1 Tatum downplays beef Knicks change ring tune Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:41 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There is a big time injury for the Los Angeles Rams . And the Raiders have a major concern as well. These teams meet in Week 7, and here are bold predictions for the NFL contest. It's a crucial game for the Rams, who stand at 2-4 and find themselves a staggering four games behind the front-running 49ers in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Raiders stand at 3-3 in third place in the AFC West. They're unlikely to be a playoff contender, but are trying to build a strong foundation for 2027. Let's take a look at what could happen when these teams battle. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Matthew Stafford will throw for three touchdowns It's hard to gauge what kind of yardage output Stafford will have. Without the injured Davante Adams, the Rams may lean on the ground game a little more. Adams is the team's leading receiver with 480 yards and four touchdowns. Sure, Stafford still has Puka Nacua. And Nacua will get his targets and yardage. But who steps into the No. 2 role? Maybe the Rams will use tight end Tyler Higbee more. Or perhaps Konata Mumpfield or Jordan Whittington will step up and produce. However, despite the receiver situation, the Rams will need to find a way to get the ball into the end zone if the Raiders load up to stop the run in the red zone. So look for Stafford to spread it around and still get his TD passes. Stafford said he understands the situation , according to The Athletic. "I just feel even more responsibility to try to be as good as I can be to help us continue to win," Stafford said. "In some of those guys' instances where they're going to have opportunities to hopefully come back and play for us, make sure that when they come back and play for us, it's meaningful stuff for them." However, some observers think Stafford has finally reached the end of his NFL rope, according to ESPN. "Stafford can't move," Ben Solak wrote. "He was never the most mobile quarterback, but the Rams were willing to use him on boots in the past. In 2024, 16.8% of Stafford's pass attempts were on the run — an above-average number! That fell to 13.9% in 2025 and is down to 9.6% in 2026. Sure, designed rollouts are down — but it isn't just that. "Stafford has zero scrambling passing yards on the season per NFL Next Gen Stats. He has yet to break the pocket and complete a pass on a scramble drill. The last quarterback to log no scramble passing yards through six weeks of a season was 2022 Tom Brady — the final season of a pocket passing titan." But it's not time to write Stafford off. Rams RB Kyren Williams will rush for 90-plus yards The Rams must run the football against the Raiders, a team that struggles to stop the ground game. The Raiders are giving up 134.3 yards per game, which ranks No. 28 in the NFL. Keeping the ball on the ground needs to be a big part of the Rams' game plan. The Rams have thrown 252 passes with 148 rushing attempts. McVay wants those numbers closer together , according to theramswire.com. "Ultimately, what I care about and what we care about is what's the best way is to move the ball and score points," McVay said. "Because of some of the situations that we've been in, those two-minute situations have gotten us a little bit out of balance. No matter how I cut it, it's an excuse. I'd like to be able to have a little bit more balance. And that's reflected by being efficient on early downs and sustaining drives." One thing is for sure, Williams and the Rams haven't lost their belief that this can be a special season. "Man, my confidence is still as high as ever," Williams said. "We know what we've got on our team and in this locker room. We come to practice every single week. That's why we can't lose our focus. We can't lose what matters the most, and that's the work. "It's about having faith. That the work we put in every single week will come to shine." Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty will split carries with Mike Washington Jr. There's no doubt that Jeanty has been a huge disappointment for the Raiders. They picked him No. 6 overall, expecting a franchise-changing player. Instead, Jeanty has a career average of 3.5 yards per carry. And Washington has been turning heads with the coaching staff, according to a post on the Raiders' YouTube page via Athlon Sports. But he needs to be better at pass protection . If both are out for that matchup, Buffalo will have to roll with Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore, and Cole Bishop as their main safety rotation, as Gardner-Johnson and Franklin both might miss that game. But for that Week 8 matchup, the Bills are going to be without a key defensive back, and not due to injury. Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was suspended by the NFL for a spitting incident during the Bills vs. Raiders game. Somehow, he's not the only Bills DB to face this suspension from the NFL. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. is joining Gardner-Johnson on suspension for spitting in the Raiders game. A second Bills DB suspended for spitting incident vs. Raiders "Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended one game today for unsportsmanlike conduct that the league said was a spitting incident vs. the Las Vegas Raiders," Schefter reports. When the Bills face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, they're going to be down a few defensive backs if these suspensions from the NFL hold up. home.headline: NFL suspends Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for 1 game for spitting at Las Vegas Raiders
home.blurb: After splitting the 2024 season between the Rams and Baltimore, White re-signed with the Bills and had 16 starts last season. He didn’t rule out another return to Buffalo after completing his one-year contract last season. Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — The NFL on Monday suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay for spitting in the direction of Las Vegas Raiders players on the field during a game a day earlier. Gardner-Johnson was ejected late in the second quarter for unsportsmanlike conduct following an exchange with a group of Raiders players, including tight end Brock Bowers. In issuing the suspension, the league cited its rule applying to “any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship.” With Buffalo (5-1) entering its bye week, Gardner-Johnson’s suspension will begin on Oct. 26 and run through Nov. 2, a day after the Bills host the Baltimore Ravens. The player has the right to appeal the suspension. Gardner-Johnson apologized to his teammates immediately following Buffalo’s 33-30 win, and has since posted a note on social media apologizing to fans. “I owe my teammates an apology and to be a man about it,” Gardner-Johnson said following the game. “You got to understand that as a grown man you can’t be doing (stuff) like that in a game,” he added. “As a vet, I’ll be better. I’ll take my consequences as it is, handle it like a man and move on.” The 28-year-old won a Super Bowl with the 2024 Philadelphia Eagles and is on his sixth team in eight seasons. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the Chicago Bears in October 2025 and appeared in 10 games with 51 total tackles. He signed a one-year contract with Buffalo in March. Coach Joe Brady referred to Gardner-Johnson’s spitting act as being “inexcusable,” and said he’s discussed the matter privately with the player. “It can’t happen. That’s not what we’re about. That’s not what the game of football is about, and he knows that,” Brady said. Gardner-Johnson arrived in Buffalo with an established reputation of being a noted trash-talker and as someone who has on occasion crossed the line with illegal hits. “I don’t need a roster of everybody being the same person,” Brady said. “Obviously, he crossed the line yesterday and that can’t happen. It won’t happen again. Personality-wise, I’m not afraid to have people who are going to try to toe the line in everything they do.” Also, the Bills are bringing back a familiar face with cornerback Tre’Davious White agreeing to sign to the team’s practice squad, a person with knowledge of discussions told The Associated Press. This weekend, Seattle will host the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Kansas City is coming off a frustrating 2025 campaign, which ended with a record of 6-11. That was the first time they had a losing season under Andy Reid, and they've already turned things around. Much of that is due to Kenneth Walker III, the former Seahawk who has been electric for the Chiefs . Seattle needs to find a way to contain Walker, while also figuring out how to get their ground game on track, which could happen with Zach Charbonnet set to return to action. If they can do that, they will have a chance to score the upset. As the game nears, let's see who the experts believe will walk away with the win this weekend. "The Chiefs, who’ve never fielded a top-15 rushing attack during Mahomes’ time as a starter, rank second with an average of 159.8 ground yards per game," Kownack wrote. "Walker leads the league with 665 rushing yards -- and that’s despite the fact that he’s played one fewer game than the next three leading rushers (Bijan Robinson, James Cook III and Derrick Henry), thanks to K.C.’s Week 5 bye. Meanwhile, the Seahawks have yet to finish a game with a 100-yard rusher, and their well-documented struggles on the ground are putting too much on Sam Darnold’s plate, as evidenced by the quarterback’s seven interceptions in the past four weeks." away.headline: Chiefs place Josh Simmons on IR, raising questions about his entire future in the NFL
away.blurb: Simmons has not played a down this season. He practiced in a limited capacity last week for the first time since reporting the injury to Burkholder. On Wednesday, the team listed him as a non-participant in practice for "back/non-injury personal reasons." In August, reporters close to the team repeatedly reported that the injury was minor and that Simmons would return by Week 1. He didn't. At this point, no one can reasonably assume Simmons will return this season after he becomes eligible. Likewise, the Chiefs cannot go into another year with Simmons as their unquestioned starting left tackle. The Kansas City Chiefs are placing left tackle Josh Simmons on injured reserve, the team announced. But the story runs deeper than a Super Bowl contender losing its starting left tackle for, most likely, the remainder of the season. On Thursday, Chiefs Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance Rich Burkholder told reporters that Simmons reported a leg issue on August 17, which the team determined was related to a bulging disc in his back. Burkholder said Simmons saw a specialist who recommended therapy instead of surgery. Burkholder said Simmons used the day to speak with his family before deciding it would be best to go on injured reserve. The designation requires Simmons to miss at least four games. Put bluntly, skepticism about the Chiefs' version of events is warranted. The next explanation was that the Chiefs had not placed him on injured reserve because they expected him to play within the first four weeks. He never did. Burkholder says Simmons "plateaued" in his recovery. If so, head coach Andy Reid was unaware. On Monday, Reid said Simmons would continue to "ramp up" this week. On Wednesday morning, Reid did not include Simmons among the players who would not practice. The team's explanation is that Reid simply forgot to mention his starting left tackle's status. Simmons' history adds another mysterious element to the situation. In fact, "mysterious" was the word ESPN NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler used to describe it last month. Fowler's comment was notable because most other top national NFL reporters have avoided the story entirely. Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport host injury-related segments throughout the week on ESPN and NFL Network, yet neither has addressed the prolonged absence of Patrick Mahomes' starting left tackle. Meanwhile, they have provided countless updates on backup linebackers and kicker competitions. "Mysterious" also describes Simmons' rookie season a year ago. He missed an entire month due to what the team called a "personal matter." ESPN reported at the time that members of the organization were unaware of why Simmons did not show up before a Week 6 matchup against the Detroit Lions. In August, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame added that Simmons left the team the night before the game and that there was a period during which the team did not know his whereabouts. home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs will head to Seattle with a depleted offensive line after right tackle Jaylon Moore was ruled out for Sunday's matchup with the Seahawks. The absence adds to a growing list of concerns surrounding Patrick Mahomes' protection. Moore did not practice Wednesday, Thursday or Friday while recovering from a concussion sustained during Kansas City's Oct. 18 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chiefs officially ruled him out for the Seattle game. Chiefs head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder said Simmons' recovery had plateaued, making the move necessary. He indicated that surgery was not being discussed at that point, while the team focused on helping the tackle return to full function. Simmons' absence had already forced Kansas City to look elsewhere for blindside protection. With him now unavailable for at least four weeks and Moore ruled out against Seattle, the team's tackle depth faces a significant test. Seattle's defense can create problems when edge rushers win quickly and force a quarterback to move before routes develop. Mahomes' ability to escape pressure helps, but constant disruption can limit the offense's timing and available options. That participation in practice is encouraging for Kansas City, but it does not solve the protection problem in front of him. The quarterback may be available without restrictions, yet still face a tougher assignment due to changes along the offensive line. The Chiefs will also be without wide receiver Rashee Rice, who was ruled out after missing practice all week with hamstring and knee issues. His absence removes another option from an offense preparing for a difficult road matchup. Tight end Travis Kelce has been limited in practice with an ankle injury but has no game designation on the final report. His availability could help, although the offense still faces the challenge of operating without Rice and a regular tackle. home.headline: Elijah Arroyo injury update: Seattle Seahawks receive devastating news as young tight end faces another major setback in promising NFL career
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Look, this injury hurts because Elijah Arroyo was just starting to carve out a role. The Seahawks took him in the second round of the 2025 NFL draft with the 50th overall pick. That’s real draft capital for a tight end. He tore his ACL in September of 2022 at Miami. That injury limited him to only nine games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. He bounced back and put together a great college career with the Hurricanes, which is a big reason Seattle used a second-round pick on him. Seahawks tight end Elijah Arroyo will miss the rest of the 2026 season, dealing another significant blow to his development after previous injury setbacks. How much more can Elijah Arroyo’s young career take? The Seattle Seahawks tight end is undergoing shoulder surgery and will miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter . Arroyo got hurt in last Thursday night’s primetime loss to the Denver Broncos as he was trying to recover a fumble by wide receiver Rashid Shaheed. It’s a brutal way to lose a season, and it’s even tougher for a second-year player who still has a lot to prove. The numbers tell the story. Arroyo will miss 11 games for Seattle, plus any potential postseason run. Seahawks fans won’t see him on the field again until 2027. Arroyo’s development takes a hit As a rookie, he played in 13 games and caught 15 passes for 179 yards and one touchdown. Those aren’t eye-popping numbers, but they’re a reasonable foundation for a first-year tight end learning the NFL game. The 2026 season hasn’t gone the way anyone hoped, though. Through six games, Arroyo had just one catch for 17 yards, obviously much less production than his rookie year. Now he won’t get the chance to turn that around. This shoulder injury is going to set him back a good bit. A second-year jump matters for young tight ends, and Arroyo loses most of that year. Losing those reps hurts. Injury history follows Arroyo from Miami to Seattle Now, Arroyo’s injury history isn’t new . It just hasn’t involved his shoulder until now. Most of his problems have been with his knee. The knee issues followed him to the NFL, though. In December 2025, Arroyo suffered a Grade One knee strain. It resulted in the Seahawks placing him on injured reserve, and him missing the rest of the season. This shoulder injury is a different animal for Elijah Arroyo. It’s the longest absence of his pro career by a wide margin. For a player who has already lost chunks of time in college and the NFL, it’s another frustrating hurdle. What it means for the Seahawks’ tight end room I’m not going to pretend this changes everything for Seattle. It’s obvious Arroyo came in to be the No. 2 tight end, even as a fairly high draft pick. The Seahawks are set at the position with AJ Barner leading the way. Seattle’s passing game will keep running through its top options, and the tight end room isn’t suddenly in crisis mode. home.blurb: Charbonnet, who sustained a torn ACL that required surgery in a divisional-round playoff victory last season, was a full participant in practice all week but nonetheless was ruled out Friday. Seattle's ground game has struggled without Charbonnet and first-round pick Jadarian Price (chest/shoulder), who has been on injured reserve since Week 2. Seahawks starting weakside linebacker Drake Thomas (ankle) will miss his second straight game. Fellow linebacker Chazz Suratt (calf) was also ruled out, while five players were dubbed questionable: backup quarterback Drew Lock (right elbow), safety Nick Emmanwori (hip) and linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee), Uchenna Nwosu (hip) and Connor O'Toole (hamstring). Chiefs right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion), wide receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring, knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring) were ruled out, while left tackle Josh Simmons (back) was moved to injured reserve midweek. Chiefs cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) are questionable. The NFL's top rusher will lead his new team, the Kansas City Chiefs (5-0), into a primetime matchup Sunday against the defending NFL champion Seahawks (3-3), for whom he won the Super Bowl MVP award last season. "I'm just focused on critiquing the mistakes we made," said Walker, referring to last weekend's sluggish 22-6 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. "Once we get to that point (Seattle), we'll see." For the soft-spoken Walker, that wasn't surprising. But others, on both teams, had plenty to say. "I know it's going to be a special moment for him to get back to the place where you kind of built your career and won a Super Bowl," Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said. "... But at the end of the day, we have to win a football game." Seahawks safety Julian Love said it's been "weird for sure" watching film of Walker break off long runs for the Chiefs. "He's doing what he did for us last season, the past bunch of seasons for the Seahawks. And he's picked up where he left off from last season," Love said. "His tape looks incredible. And so it's all hands on deck to try to contain and try to stop him." Walker, who signed a three-year, $43.05 million deal with the Chiefs in the offseason as a free agent, leads all NFL running backs with 665 yards rushing and 6.3 yards per attempt. His six rushing touchdowns are two behind Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, though he's played in one fewer game because of Kansas City's early bye week. Walker rushed for 135 yards on 27 carries in the Seahawks' 29-13 victory against New England in the Super Bowl. His desire to be a true No. 1, workhorse back led him to Kansas City after splitting carries with Zach Charbonnet during most of his time in Seattle. "He's wired to do it," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said. "When you're on a team, everybody knows your strengths and weaknesses and quirks and everything. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. That was ... interesting to see. The 49ers have found a way to keep winning games despite all of the injuries. Nick Bosa , Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , Upton Stout and Mykel Williams were among the players who did not practice on Wednesday. This week, I'm going to take the points with Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 22, Falcons 20 Dubin (49ers -3): This line feels several points too low, even with Mike Evans potentially out in addition to all of the other wide receiver issues. So long as the Niners have Kyle Shanahan calling plays and Brock Purdy , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle involved, I think their offense cooks. And Atlanta can't quite reach the same level offensively — even with Bijan Robinson and Drake London on hand. The Niners have been excellent against the run this year, and if this game winds up being one where Penix has to match Purdy throw for throw, I don't see that going well for Atlanta. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Falcons 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Baltimore Ravens (-3) Dajani ( Bengals +3): The Bengals are fresh off their bye while the Baltimore Ravens are fresh off ... a loss to the Cleveland Browns . It was their 15th loss when leading by at least seven points in the fourth quarter since 2020, which ranks the most in the NFL. Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this week, but I'm curious to see how "spry" he looks. The two-time NFL MVP was playing some fantastic ball before the unfortunate ankle injury, and it's worth mentioning he's 7-2 in his career against Joe Burrow . I was high on the Bengals entering this season, and I'm not ready to move off that take. I think this Baltimore secondary is in for a tough test in stopping Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The former averages 120.4 receiving yards per game vs. the Ravens, while the latter caught two touchdowns the last time he faced them. Higgins actually hasn't faced Baltimore since Oct. 6, 2024! It's been a while. Give me the upset here. We aren't 100% sure if Jackson is even returning to the lineup, and he'll have to face one of the best interior pass rushes in the NFL. Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen and Kris Jenkins Jr. are the only defensive tackle trio to record multiple sacks this season. … Prediction: Bengals 29, Ravens 27 Dubin (Ravens -3): I'm assuming that Lamar Jackson is back for this game. If he's not, then you can switch my pick to the Bengals. If Jackson is in alongside Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers , I just don't think this Baltimore offense can be stopped. When those three have shared the field this season, the Ravens are averaging 9.9 yards per play. NINE POINT NINE. Unfortunately, the sample size is only 63 plays due to injuries to Jackson and Flowers at different times. If there is any team that can compete with an explosive offense, it's probably the Bengals, but I don't see them quite keeping up here. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bengals 26 Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani ( Lions -3): Just take the Over in this matchup. The Lions really burned me coming off the bye last year, losing to J.J. McCarthy , but I'm going to back them in this spot. The concern is, of course, the defense, which ranks dead last in the NFL with 404.4 total yards surrendered per game. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. away.blurb: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were ruled out on the final injury report released Saturday afternoon. Smith is set to miss his third game of the season because of his lingering hamstring issue, while Wicks will miss his first. Wicks, the 25-year-old receiver, appeared to injure an ankle late in the Eagles’ loss to the Carolina Panthers . Without Wicks, the Eagles will call on Makai Lemon to step up. The first-round rookie receiver out of Southern Cal said Friday that Monday’s game will provide him with a “big opportunity.” “I’m just super excited to go out there with the guys,” Lemon said. “Put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So just trying to go out there and execute. Couple guys are out, so really just next man up. I’ve got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me. Trust in the coaches and the game plan. So I’m definitely excited for this week’s matchup.” Meanwhile, running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable for Monday’s game after missing the last two contests with a hamstring injury. He said Thursday that he would “love” to make his return against the Cowboys. He was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert is available. He did not practice Thursday or Friday, but he returned on Saturday as a full participant. Goedert said Saturday that the knee injury he has been dealing with is the same one that sidelined him for two games earlier this season. He said he had “a little bit of inflammation in there,” but once it settled down, he felt good enough to return to practice. “Just making sure I tested out there full speed, but it felt good,” Goedert said. “For me, it’s just really letting the coaches know that I’m good and be able to be out there for whatever they need me for.” The Eagles also are banged up defensively. Edge rusher Nolan Smith (concussion) was ruled out on Saturday’s injury report. He did not practice all week. Defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen) also was ruled out and will miss his second straight game. Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is listed as questionable. He said Saturday that he would be a game-time decision as he deals with what he described as an ankle sprain. Greenard practiced Thursday as a limited participant and did not practice Friday or Saturday, but he refuted the notion that he experienced a setback. Greenard, who signed a four-year, $100 million deal with the Eagles upon being traded from the Minnesota Vikings in April , has been active for just three games this season. A pectoral strain kept him sidelined throughout training camp and the start of the season, and now the ankle injury has him in and out of the lineup. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) also is questionable. Hunt, the Eagles’ 2024 third-rounder out of Houston Christian, was injured in the Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and missed last week’s game against the Panthers. away.headline: Eagles face mounting injury concerns ahead of Monday night vs. Cowboys
away.blurb: Greenard, who was listed as limited Thursday with an ankle injury, did not practice Friday. He joined outside linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen). Saquon Barkley remained listed as limited with a hamstring injury after missing the past two games. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards on 36 carries, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt through four appearances. His return would give Philadelphia an important option against Dallas, though Friday’s participation won't settle his game availability. Landon Dickerson was listed as limited for a second consecutive day with knee and pectoral injuries. The left guard dinged his pectoral muscle during Thursday’s practice, adding another issue as Philadelphia attempts to stabilize its offensive line. Center Drew Kendall moved from limited to full participation despite a knee injury. Willie Lampkin returned from an illness but was listed as limited, while Fred Johnson was added to the report as limited because of an illness. AJ Epenesa, Jalyx Hunt, Moro Ojomo and Tyler Steen also remained limited. Philadelphia has another practice Saturday before issuing its final game designations. The Philadelphia Eagles listed six players as nonparticipants Friday, with Jonathan Greenard taking a step backward and several key offensive weapons remaining sidelined ahead of Monday night’s matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. The receiving injuries complicate preparations for Tanner McKee, who completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions against Carolina. Wicks has 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season, making his availability another significant concern for an offense trying to end Philadelphia’s four-game losing streak. Wicks, the 25-year-old receiver, appeared to injure an ankle late in the Eagles’ loss to the Carolina Panthers . Without Wicks, the Eagles will call on Makai Lemon to step up. The first-round rookie receiver out of Southern Cal said Friday that Monday’s game will provide him with a “big opportunity.” “I’m just super excited to go out there with the guys,” Lemon said. “Put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So just trying to go out there and execute. Couple guys are out, so really just next man up. I’ve got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me. Trust in the coaches and the game plan. So I’m definitely excited for this week’s matchup.” Meanwhile, running back Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable for Monday’s game after missing the last two contests with a hamstring injury. He said Thursday that he would “love” to make his return against the Cowboys. He was a full participant in Saturday’s practice. Tight end Dallas Goedert is available. He did not practice Thursday or Friday, but he returned on Saturday as a full participant. Goedert said Saturday that the knee injury he has been dealing with is the same one that sidelined him for two games earlier this season. He said he had “a little bit of inflammation in there,” but once it settled down, he felt good enough to return to practice. “Just making sure I tested out there full speed, but it felt good,” Goedert said. “For me, it’s just really letting the coaches know that I’m good and be able to be out there for whatever they need me for.” The Eagles also are banged up defensively. Edge rusher Nolan Smith (concussion) was ruled out on Saturday’s injury report. He did not practice all week. Defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen) also was ruled out and will miss his second straight game. Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is listed as questionable. He said Saturday that he would be a game-time decision as he deals with what he described as an ankle sprain. Greenard practiced Thursday as a limited participant and did not practice Friday or Saturday, but he refuted the notion that he experienced a setback. Greenard, who signed a four-year, $100 million deal with the Eagles upon being traded from the Minnesota Vikings in April , has been active for just three games this season. A pectoral strain kept him sidelined throughout training camp and the start of the season, and now the ankle injury has him in and out of the lineup. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) also is questionable. Hunt, the Eagles’ 2024 third-rounder out of Houston Christian, was injured in the Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and missed last week’s game against the Panthers. home.blurb: This includes the return of cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, both of whom have missed multiple weeks due to hamstring injuries. Durant has been out since getting injured in Week 2's win over the Washington Commanders while Overshown suffered his injury in Week 1 against the New York Giants. The Dallas Cowboys are heading into Week 7's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles facing what should be viewed as a must-win and should-win game. Philadelphia is dealing with major injury issues, which includes the concerning blood cot issues for quarterback Jalen Hurt along with wide receiver DeVonta Smith's lingering hamstring injury. Both players will miss Week 7 against Dallas. The Cowboys had multiple names on the injury report themselves this week, but fortunately, Dallas is looking fairly healthy across the board headed into Monday Night Football. Good News for George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr. The Cowboys released their final injury report before Monday Night Football, and some of the team's most important players are good to go for the game. Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder) and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) are both without an injury designation and will play against the Eagles. Both players are in a contract year and still have a lot to prove to the Dallas front office. They can't afford to miss any games both for their individual goals and if the Cowboys want any chance at winning the NFC East. Key Players Returning for Cowboys Defense Additionally, the Cowboys are officially getting back some key players on defense ahead of Week 7. home.blurb: Ex-Eagles WR A.J. Brown Called Out for ‘Giving Up' on New Team Eagles-Jalen Hurts Situation Could Spark Major Change Amid NFL Investigation Unlock the latest Heavy on Eagles news — direct to your inbox. There was some early confusion following the initial reports of the health status of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts following the team's loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Hurts reportedly had a blood clot in his leg but was cleared to play against Jacksonville provided he get a follow-up scan of his leg. It was then revealed that Hurts' blood clot had moved, causing major concern. Ultimately, it was revealed he had blood clots in his lungs, which will force him to miss the rest of the season. It also prompted many to wonder if the Eagles' medical staff had done things properly in how they handled Hurts' situation. Insider Says Eagles-Hurts Situation Could Spark Change Getty Philadelphia Eagles QB Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season due to blood clots in his lungs On Saturday, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones revealed that because there's still many questions left unanswered about how the Eagles handled Hurts' health, it could force the NFL to change how certain injuries are reported and followed-up with, specifically blood clot issues. "The NFL Players Association seeks a full investigation into the handling of Jalen Hurts' medical situation. That will take time. But even if it is determined everything was handled properly and this was an unfortunate episode, it could still bring about change. "… While there are surely recommended medical practices, there isn't a collectively bargained league protocol on how to handle players with some form of clotting, regarding either playing or traveling to games. But perhaps the seriousness of blood clots and, frankly, the popularity of this player may create some sort of protocol. If the game is domestic, would a player like Hurts still have flown back? "Would there be private travel that could land in an emergency? If the game is international, like it was, what becomes the standard? Even if nothing untoward is found in this investigation, it could still bring rise to an established set of protocols the league winds up following for domestic and international contests." NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell Welcomes Investigation Getty NFL commissioner Roger Goodell says he welcomes an investigation into the Eagles-Jalen Hurts situation After Hurts' season-ending diagnosis was announced, the NFL Players' Association immediately issued a statement calling for an investigation into how the Eagles handled the situation. "The NFLPA is not aware of any NFL investigation into the medical care provided to Jalen Hurts," the statement read . "In fact, the league previously informed the union that it did not plan to review the care he received. home.headline: Eagles face mounting injury concerns ahead of Monday night vs. Cowboys
home.blurb: Greenard, who was listed as limited Thursday with an ankle injury, did not practice Friday. He joined outside linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion), wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen). Saquon Barkley remained listed as limited with a hamstring injury after missing the past two games. Barkley has rushed for 182 yards on 36 carries, averaging 5.1 yards per attempt through four appearances. His return would give Philadelphia an important option against Dallas, though Friday’s participation won't settle his game availability. Landon Dickerson was listed as limited for a second consecutive day with knee and pectoral injuries. The left guard dinged his pectoral muscle during Thursday’s practice, adding another issue as Philadelphia attempts to stabilize its offensive line. Center Drew Kendall moved from limited to full participation despite a knee injury. Willie Lampkin returned from an illness but was listed as limited, while Fred Johnson was added to the report as limited because of an illness. AJ Epenesa, Jalyx Hunt, Moro Ojomo and Tyler Steen also remained limited. Philadelphia has another practice Saturday before issuing its final game designations. The Philadelphia Eagles listed six players as nonparticipants Friday, with Jonathan Greenard taking a step backward and several key offensive weapons remaining sidelined ahead of Monday night’s matchup against the Dallas Cowboys. The receiving injuries complicate preparations for Tanner McKee, who completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions against Carolina. Wicks has 19 receptions for 284 yards and a touchdown this season, making his availability another significant concern for an offense trying to end Philadelphia’s four-game losing streak.
